_comment: Batch 021-R -- arch_duct evidence only.
The owner passed five of the six 021 modules and held arch_duct for
one reason: S_services_family renders it edge-on and small beside the
vent, so silhouette, construction, attachment and section seams were
not actually reviewable. This is that evidence and nothing else --
the asset is unchanged.
Two shots, matching the two things that could not be judged:
R_duct_detail    close three-quarter. The flange at each end and at
mid-run is what stops a 4 m run reading as a long
box, and it is the part the family shot lost.
R_duct_run       three sections chained under two ceiling bays. The
duct module is 4.0 m and arch_ceiling_plain is
4.0 x 4.0, so sections and bays share one grid --
which is the claim a repeated-section shot has to
test. It also shows the hangers meeting the ceiling
they hang from, which is the attachment question.
Both are `frame` cameras, which solve their own distance from the
subject AABB and cannot miss it (L-62).

Both shots use backdrop 'none'. arch_duct and arch_ceiling_plain are CEILING anchored -- their geometry hangs below the origin -- so the runner's default floor slab sits on top of them and the first attempt rendered a tilted grey plane with two dark specks on it. That is L-63 again: an asset that is not an object standing on a floor must not be given a floor to stand on.

R_duct_run is shot from BELOW (negative elevation). The first attempt used +10 and rendered the top face of the ceiling bays with the ducts hidden underneath -- a view no player will ever have of a ceiling service.
